comparison: Perfect agreement on claims C4, C12-C17 regarding the mutagenesis screen methodology and F876L identification. Both evaluations found the data convincing, comprehensive, and well-documented with no methodological concerns.

Both address claims C27-C30, C59 on spontaneous mutation acquisition. OpenEval found the deep sequencing data sufficient, while peer reviewers raised concerns about the incomplete mutational landscape, questioning why other AR mutations in resistant tumors weren't fully characterized.
Complete agreement on claims C31-C32 regarding systematic mutagenesis data showing residue 876's importance. Both evaluations found this SAR data convincing with no concerns raised.

Both evaluate claims C33-C34, C69 on bicalutamide behavior. OpenEval found the data supported the claims, but peer reviewers noted inconsistencies in whether bicalutamide acts as agonist or antagonist across different figures, creating uncertainty.

Strong agreement on claims C6, C35-C41, C70-C75 regarding the structural mechanism. Both found the MD simulations insufficient without experimental validation. Peer reviewers specifically noted unclear interactions between F876L and ligands, requesting additional structural data.

Both address novel compound validation (C7, C43-C52, C63). OpenEval found the in vitro data comprehensive and sufficient. Peer reviewers found it of high interest but noted missing xenograft validation, binding affinity measurements, and enantiomer separation studies.

Both address pharmacological characterization with substantial overlap (C18-C22 in OpenEval; C5, C18-C26, C58 in peer review). Both found the functional resistance and agonist conversion data convincing and comprehensive with no challenges.

Partial overlap on in vitro/in vivo validation (C5, C23-C26). Both evaluations found this data convincing across multiple cell lines and xenograft models, with peer reviewers praising the comprehensive documentation.
Both address claim C76 on enantiomer differences for DR103. Complete agreement that this is speculative and requires experimental validation through enantiomer separation and testing.
Overlap on computational predictions for DR103 (C53-C55). Both found these claims require experimental validation, with peer reviewers requesting binding affinity data and in vivo testing.
OpenEval evaluated background/context claims C1-C3, C8-C10, C56 establishing clinical and scientific rationale. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these foundational claims.
OpenEval evaluated claims C11, C57, C64 on BCR-ABL precedent for mutagenesis screening. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these methodological precedent claims.
OpenEval evaluated claim C81 on proof-of-concept validation experiment. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this technical feasibility claim.
Minimal overlap on synthesis claims C58, C60. Both found the characterization of F876L as a gain-of-function mechanism well-supported by the experimental data.

OpenEval evaluated claims C61-C62, C88 citing prior work on progesterone receptor and medicinal chemistry rationale. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these literature citation claims.
OpenEval evaluated claims C65-C66 on blood-based detection proposals. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these speculative future direction claims.
OpenEval evaluated claims C67-C68, C80 on clinical context from literature. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these background clinical claims.
OpenEval evaluated claims C77-C79 on future applications of MD simulations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these prospective utility claims.
OpenEval evaluated claim C42 on computational predictions consistent with SAR data. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for this specific structural prediction claim.
